Waiting would cost ~$1,031,297 (3596s remaining) and EXCEEDS the 60s tolerance (BIZ-5). Terminating costs a 95-minute replay of inventory_month_end_close (policy may_interrupt, BIZ-2). audit.report: The month-end close job (inventory_month_end_close, pid 93126) sat idle in transaction for 4 seconds while holding locks that blocked checkout, collapsing success to 6% over 30 seconds against a 95% SLO and putting $17,207/min of revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker, citing a trade-off where waiting would cost ~$1,031,297 in lost checkout revenue versus a 95-minute replay of the batch job. The Continuity Guardian escalated because an active change calendar (CHG-4410) requires finance-ops owner consultation before interrupting this workload. The incident ended in escalation after 79.9 seconds with no action executed; checkout remained degraded and the business tolerance of 60 seconds was exceeded.
audit.root_cause: An idle-in-transaction batch worker (batch_replayable_month_end_close) held locks that blocked checkout, and the required owner consultation under CHG-4410 prevented immediate termination.
lessons: Add a pre-approved termination rule for inventory_month_end_close during checkout degradation so the Database Guardian can act without waiting for finance-ops consultation.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly identified the blocker and quantified the trade-off in round 1, but the Continuity Guardian properly invoked invariant I3 and escalated due to the consult_owner policy on CHG-4410; neither guardian wasted a round, but the process stalled because the required human decision could not arrive within the 60-second business tolerance.
follow_ups: Finance-ops to confirm or update the consult_owner policy for CHG-4410 and define a default action when they are unreachable.
